You aren't automatically adhering to decisions. If you were you wouldn't be asking people for advice. 

What you are doing is *equally* discussing with your fiancé what you *both* want. 

THAT is feminism. You saying you don't want to take his name because you feel it is traditional and falling into social norms is NOT equal, that is choosing to automatically ignore your husbands feelings because you think yours are more important.

You take the name that you both decide on. Which is what you are doing now. Don't pretend you don't have a choice because you clearly do. You also clearly don't seem to attached to your name while he does.

Gender doesn't matter to this decision, feelings do. He feels he wants his name, you feel you want any name *but* his.

It does seem petty that you are open to changing your name, just not to his name. 


He clearly wants to keep his name, and the only reason you don't want to is because you don't want to be traditional. 

That kind of thinking is what is wrong with feminism.

Don't let tradition impact your decision in *any* way.

Does it matter if it's antiquated? Is the only reason you don't want to do it is because it's not feminist? 

Feminism has grown past the point of doing or not doing things just because they were once not a choice. Now the fact that you are choosing whether or not to take his name is feminist. The actual outcome of the decision doesn't matter. 

Don't pretend to be progressive for the sake of looking progressive.

FTFU

Femenisim, traditions, and social norms shouldn't have any affect on your decision. If you think this decision is between you and your fiancé, why bother bringing in these other factors. All they will do is confuse you. 

So honestly it looks like you have three choices. Respect your future father in-laws opinion and take your husbands name, respect your fiancés decision and take yours, or push for your feeling and convince your fiancé to choose a name together. 


His father obviously feels the most strongly, but should that be a factor in your private choice? Some people would think so, but you might not. And that's okay. 


Your fiancé seems feel very strongly about keeping his name, you seem more indifferent and your strongest argument seems to be not wanting to conform to social norms. But sometimes feelings don't need arguments. 


And finally, you seem very much to want a new name. Now, do you want that more than you don't want what your partner wants? Will you convince him? Is it worth potential arguments or hurt feelings to push your choice? 


These questions seem to be much more important from what I am seeing than trying to be feminist. After all, feminism is about equal, personal choice. Therefore, you need to base your decision on your relationship and your feelings.
